title: The I/O commands of the Sound Blaster DSP
covers: the commands a host writes to the command port of a Sound Blaster DSP, as Creative's hardware programming guide describes them and as DOSBox-X decodes them

rows.text: Command 10h plays digitized sound one byte at a time in 8-bit direct mode.
The command is followed by one data byte, bData.
The data byte the program sends is one byte of unsigned digitized sound data.
The application is responsible for controlling the sampling rate.
The programmer sends the command and a data byte at the timing the sound needs, repeating until all data is sent.
It repeats the sample up to three times when the mixer buffer holds under 40 ms and keeps the byte in dac.last_direct_dac.
DOSBox-X estimates the rate from the interval since the previous write and caps it at 1 kHz.
It programs the ESS filter dividers from 22050 Hz and sets the mixer frequency to the estimated rate.
A direct DAC byte written while the speaker is off logs a warning, once, then stops logging it.
Command 14h plays digitized sound output by 8-bit single-cycle DMA mode.
The command is followed by wLength low byte then high byte, the 8-bit samples to play less 1.
The data output is digitized sound, sent by single-cycle DMA mode.
The data output is unsigned digitized sound.
Command 24h records digitized sound input by 8-bit single-cycle DMA mode.
The command is followed by wLength low byte then high byte, the 8-bit samples to record less 1.
The data recorded is digitized sound, taken by single-cycle DMA mode.
The data recorded is unsigned digitized sound.
Command 99h records digitized sound input by 8-bit high-speed single-cycle DMA mode.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
The guide's title calls command 91h an 8-bit high-speed single-cycle DMA mode digitized sound input command.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
After a block of data of the size command 48h set, the DSP generates an interrupt and exits high-speed mode.
DOSBox-X treats 91h as an output command, sharing the code of 14h and clearing the recording flag.
The block size comes from the two data bytes left by an earlier command, not from command 48h.
At the end of a single-cycle block the card raises its IRQ and clears high-speed mode.
Command 98h records digitized sound input by 8-bit high-speed auto-init DMA mode.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
Command 90h plays digitized sound output by 8-bit high-speed auto-init DMA mode.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
The DSP generates an interrupt after every block of the size command 48h set.
In high-speed mode the DSP will not accept any other commands.
To end high-speed mode, the programmer sends a DSP reset command.
The reset ends high-speed mode and restores all DSP parameters to their state before it was entered.
DOSBox-X ignores commands in high-speed mode only for a card that is not an SB16 and has no ESS or Reveal SC400 emulation.
The reset puts fixed defaults back: 22050 Hz, time constant 45, last direct DAC value 0x80.
Command 2Ch records digitized sound input by 8-bit auto-init DMA mode.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
The data recorded is digitized sound, taken by auto-init DMA mode.
The data recorded is unsigned digitized sound.
Command 1Ch plays digitized sound output by 8-bit auto-init DMA mode.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
The data output is digitized sound, sent by auto-init DMA mode.
The data output is unsigned digitized sound.
The DSP generates an interrupt after transferring every block of the size command 48h set.
The programmer ends auto-init I/O by programming single-cycle I/O or by sending the exit command, both at the end of the current block.
Command 1Fh plays 8-bit to 2-bit ADPCM output with the reference byte, by auto-init DMA mode.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
The data output is compressed with Creative 8-bit to 2-bit ADPCM and sent by auto-init DMA mode.
To end the transfer the programmer follows command 1Ch; a last block played single-cycle uses the command without reference byte, 16h.
Command 17h plays 8-bit to 2-bit ADPCM single-cycle DMA output with the reference byte.
The command is followed by wLength low byte then high byte, the bytes to transfer less 1.
The first block of digitized sound is compressed with Creative 8-bit to 2-bit ADPCM and sent by single-cycle DMA.
The programmer sends the following blocks with the no reference byte command.
Command 74h plays Creative 8-bit to 4-bit ADPCM single-cycle DMA output.
The command is followed by wLength low byte then high byte, as command 16h describes.
The output is Creative 8-bit to 4-bit ADPCM sent by single-cycle DMA mode, as command 16h describes.
Command 75h plays Creative 8-bit to 4-bit ADPCM single-cycle DMA output with the reference byte.
The command is followed by wLength low byte then high byte, as command 17h describes.
The first block of Creative 8-bit to 4-bit ADPCM is sent by single-cycle DMA, as command 17h describes.
Command 76h plays Creative 8-bit to 3-bit ADPCM single-cycle DMA output.
The command is followed by wLength low byte then high byte, as command 16h describes.
The output is Creative 8-bit to 3-bit ADPCM sent by single-cycle DMA mode, as command 16h describes.
Command 77h plays Creative 8-bit to 3-bit ADPCM single-cycle DMA output with the reference byte.
The command is followed by wLength low byte then high byte, as command 17h describes.
The first block of Creative 8-bit to 3-bit ADPCM is sent by single-cycle DMA, as command 17h describes.
Command 7Dh plays Creative 8-bit to 4-bit ADPCM auto-init DMA output with the reference byte.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
The data is Creative 8-bit to 4-bit ADPCM sent by auto-init DMA with the reference byte, as command 1Fh describes.
Command 7Fh plays Creative 8-bit to 3-bit ADPCM auto-init DMA output with the reference byte.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
The data is Creative 8-bit to 3-bit ADPCM sent by auto-init DMA mode, as command 1Fh describes.
Command 38h outputs MIDI data to the MIDI port in non-UART mode.
The command is followed by the MIDI data byte the programmer sends.
The programmer sends the command and then the MIDI data.
No byte reaches the MIDI port when MIDI is turned off for the card.
Command 40h sets the digitized sound transfer time constant.
The command is followed by one byte, bTimeConstant.
The time constant is the DSP's rate representation: 65536 minus 256000000 over channels times rate, channels 1 mono and 2 stereo.
The programmer sends only the high byte of the computed result to the DSP.
On an ESS board the filter is updated from the new rate.
Command 41h sets the digitized sound output sampling rate.
The command is followed by wSamplingRate high byte then low byte.
The DSP's valid sampling rates run from 5000 to 45000 Hz inclusive.
The programmer does not pre-multiply the rate by two for stereo as the time constant requires.
DOSBox-X takes any 16-bit rate, and limits playback to 5000 to 45454 Hz only when sample-rate limits are enabled.
DOSBox-X clears the time-constant flag and mirrors the rate into SB16 memory bytes 0x13 and 0x14.
Command 42h sets the digitized sound input sampling rate.
The command is followed by wSamplingRate high byte then low byte.
DOSBox-X clears the time-constant flag and mirrors the rate into SB16 memory bytes 0x13 and 0x14.
Command 48h sets the DSP block transfer size.
The DSP generates an interrupt after transferring the block of data, the number of bytes to transfer less 1.
The command is followed by wBlockSize low byte then high byte.
The programmer uses this command with high-speed mode and auto-init DMA mode.
In 16-bit DMA mode DOSBox-X halves the count, warning when the byte count is odd.

rows.text: On an SB16 command 04h stores the data byte in ASP_mode, the ASP mode register.
Bit 2 of the stored mode resets the ASP memory index; the comments say bit 7 with bit 3 enables memory access and bits 1 and 0 step the index.
On a Sound Blaster 2 the command returns 0x88, on a Pro 0x7b, and on any other card 0xFF.
The command is followed by one data byte, which becomes the ASP mode register on an SB16.

When ASP is not enabled, the same subcommand returns 0xFF.
Any other subcommand, and any card that is not an SB16, is logged as unhandled.
The command is followed by a subcommand byte; 03 asks for the chip version.

rows.text: With ASP enabled on an SB16, command 0Eh stores the second data byte in ASP_regs at the first.
Register 0x83 with mode bits 7 and 3 set takes the memory path, and mode bit 2 resets its index.
The byte is written into ASP internal RAM at the index, which advances when mode bit 1 is set.
Register 0x83 without both mode bits is logged as not implemented and writes nothing.
Any other register reaches no memory path and is only logged.
With ASP not enabled the write is ignored and logged.
On a card that is not an SB16 the command is logged as unhandled.
The command is followed by two data bytes: the register number and the value.

rows.text: Command 0Fh reads an ASP register on an SB16, whether or not ASP emulation is enabled.
Register 0x83 with mode bits 7 and 3 set reads the internal RAM byte at the index into ASP_regs[0x83].
Mode bit 0 advances the ASP memory index after the read.
Register 0x83 without both mode bits returns 0x10, the ASP chip version.
The byte chosen is queued for the host to read.
Any other register, or ASP disabled, is logged and takes no memory path.
On a card that is not an SB16 the command is logged as unhandled.
The command is followed by one data byte, the register number it reads.

rows.text: Command 15h is handled exactly as command 14h: an 8-bit single-cycle DMA output transfer.
The two parameter bytes are taken as the block length, as command 14h takes them.
Command 16h plays single-cycle DMA output of digitized sound compressed 8-bit to 2-bit ADPCM.
The command is followed by wLength low byte then high byte.
Subsequent blocks are compressed 8-bit to 2-bit ADPCM and sent by single-cycle DMA.
wLength is a word giving the number of bytes to transfer less 1.
The programmer transfers the first block with the reference byte command.
Command 80h pauses digitized sound output for a duration.
The command is followed by wDuration low byte then high byte.
wDuration gives the pause in units of the sampling period less 1.
When the specified duration elapses, the DSP generates an interrupt.
Command A0h sets the input mode to mono.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
The default input mode is mono.
DOSBox-X accepts A0h only on SB Pro models; on others it logs a warning and leaves the mixer as it was.
Command Bxh programs 16-bit DMA mode digitized sound I/O.
The command is followed by bMode, then wLength low byte and high byte.
bCommand is 1011 in bits 7-4; bits 3-0 are A/D, auto-init, FIFO and 0, and a new I/O command re-initializes the FIFO.
bMode holds stereo in bit 5 and signed in bit 4.
The signed bit selects signed or unsigned data; minimum amplitude is 0000h signed and 8000h unsigned.
wLength is the number of 16-bit samples less 1.
The programmer ends auto-init DMA mode as command 1Ch says.
Cxh programs 8-bit DMA mode and is followed by bCommand, bMode and wLength; its bCommand differs only in the high nibble 1100.
For 8-bit data the minimum amplitude is 00h signed and 80h unsigned.
wLength is the number of 8-bit samples less 1.
On an ESS card A0h-CFh is handled before the switch: a write below C0h and a C0h read of register A0h-BFh need extended mode.
On a Reveal SC400 only B6h, BEh, C6h and CEh are accepted; every other command of the range is logged and ignored.
C6h and C7h set and clear extended mode; any other command of the range is logged as unknown.
Command D0h pauses 8-bit DMA mode digitized sound I/O.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
After the command the DSP ceases to send out DMA requests.
It applies to both single-cycle and auto-init DMA modes.
Command D5h pauses 16-bit DMA mode digitized sound I/O.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
It acts on I/O initiated by command Bxh, in both single-cycle and auto-init modes.
Command D1h turns the digitized sound output speaker on.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
The speaker is the connection of the digitized output to the amplifier input, with no effect on FM music.
The DSP takes at most 112 milliseconds to complete the command.
On version 1.xx the DSP pauses the DMA transfer after the command.
On version 4.xx it has no practical output effect, but sets the internal speaker flag on for command D8h.
DOSBox-X changes the speaker at once, with no wait of up to 112 ms.
DOSBox-X does not pause the DMA transfer on a version 1.xx card.
Command D3h turns the digitized sound output speaker off.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
The DSP takes at most 220 milliseconds to complete the command.
On version 1.xx the DSP pauses the DMA transfer after the command.
On version 4.xx it has no practical output effect, but sets the internal speaker flag off for command D8h.
DOSBox-X changes the speaker at once, with no wait of up to 220 ms.
DOSBox-X sets the speaker flag off as the row says, and logs a warning when an SB16 with DMA running gets the command.
The case calls FillUp and DSP_SetSpeaker(false) at src/hardware/sblaster.cpp:2365-2366 before the conditional log at 2383.
Command D8h gets the digitized sound output speaker status.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
The DSP returns FFh when the speaker is on and 00h when it is off.
Command D6h continues 16-bit DMA mode digitized sound I/O.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
It acts on I/O initiated by command Bxh, in both single-cycle and auto-init modes.
Command D4h continues 8-bit DMA mode digitized sound I/O.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
It resumes the transfer command D0h paused, in both single-cycle and auto-init modes.
Command D9h exits 16-bit auto-init DMA mode digitized sound I/O.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
It exits at the end of the current 16-bit auto-init block and terminates the I/O process.
Command DAh exits 8-bit auto-init DMA mode digitized sound I/O.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
It exits at the end of the current 8-bit auto-init block and terminates the I/O process.
Command E1h gets the DSP version number.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
The DSP returns two bytes: the major version, then the minor.
A Sound Blaster 1.0 answers 1.0, a 1.5 answers 1.5, a 2.0 answers 2.0 and a later 2.0 answers 2.1.
On a Media Vision PAS it alternates between 1.48 and 2.0.
A Sound Blaster Pro answers 3.0 or 3.2, an ESS Pro 3.1 and an SC400 its stored version.
An SB16 answers 4.5, 4.12 with an AWE32 and 4.13 with a ViBRA.

rows.text: Command F8h flushes the output buffer and returns one zero byte.
The command takes no data byte.
Command 30h inputs MIDI data by polling.
Commands 30h and 31h are sent with no parameter byte.
In polling mode the programmer sends command 30h and then polls the DSP for MIDI data.
Command 31h inputs MIDI data by interrupt.
The programmer sends command 31h again to terminate the mode.
In interrupt mode the DSP interrupts the application when in-bound MIDI data arrives after command 31h.
DOSBox-X logs an unimplemented MIDI I/O command for 30h to 33h and does nothing else.
Command 34h enters UART polling mode for MIDI I/O.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
In UART mode a read from the DSP is taken as reading MIDI data.
In UART mode a write to the DSP is taken as sending MIDI data.
The programmer ends UART mode with a DSP reset, which restores the parameters the DSP had before it entered.
A read hands back a byte of the DSP output buffer, where command replies are queued.
Command 35h enters UART interrupt mode.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
After the command the DSP interrupts when in-bound MIDI data arrives.
DOSBox-X arms the polling and read-interrupt flags and returns.
Command 20h inputs digitized sound one byte at a time in 8-bit direct mode.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
A read from the DSP gives one byte of unsigned digitized sound data.
The application is responsible for controlling the sampling rate.
The programmer repeats the command and the read at the timing the recording needs.
A build without Windows microphone support queues the fixed byte 0x7F for the read; a Windows build queues a sample only with the microphone recording source and a microphone present.
Command 37h runs UART interrupt mode MIDI I/O with time stamping.
The command is sent with no parameter byte.
After the command the DSP interrupts the application when in-bound MIDI data arrives.
The DSP time stamps in-bound MIDI data.
On an SB2 or above DOSBox-X sets the polling, read-interrupt and time-stamp flags and raises no interrupt; an SB 1.x logs that the command needs SB2.
On an SB2 or above DOSBox-X records time-stamp mode in a flag; an SB 1.x logs that the command needs SB2, and the case queues no time stamp.

rows.text: With the SC400 reveal enabled, command E6h registers a DMA callback on the 8-bit channel and sets the DSP output to 0x80.
Outside the SC400 reveal the command returns without registering the callback.
When the channel is unmasked the callback writes the eight-byte pattern 01 02 04 08 10 20 40 80 and raises the 8-bit IRQ.
The command is sent with no data byte.

rows.text: With the SC400 reveal enabled, command 50h stores its data byte as the card configuration.
Outside the SC400 reveal the command returns before reading the byte.
Bits 1-0 select the 8-bit DMA channel, 1, 2 and 3 choosing channels 0, 1 and 3 and 0 choosing none.
The 16-bit DMA channel is set to the same one as the 8-bit.
Bits 5-3 select the IRQ, values 1 to 5 choosing 7, 9, 10, 11 and 5 and the others choosing none.
Bit 2 enables the MPU-401 IRQ, which bit 7 selects as 9 or 5; a changed MPU IRQ logs a warning that MPU-401 emulation does not yet support changing it.
The new configuration byte and the resulting IRQ and DMA channel are logged.
One data byte follows the command.

rows.text: With the SC400 reveal enabled, command 58h queues three bytes for the read: the two jumper status bytes and the configuration byte.
Outside the SC400 reveal the command returns without queuing a byte.
The first status byte is 2Ch plus 1 when the base port is 240h and plus 2 when both gameports are disabled.
The second status byte holds C0h and four bits of the card's base port plus 10h shifted right four, which the comment calls the CD-ROM port's bits 8-4.
The configuration byte starts at 0 and is built from the card's DMA channel, IRQ and MPU-401 IRQ at initialisation.
The command is sent with no data byte.

rows.text: With the SC400 reveal enabled, command 6Eh stores its two data bytes as the SC400's DSP major and minor version.
Outside the SC400 reveal the command returns without storing a version.
Command E1h reports the stored major and minor version on an SC400.
Two data bytes follow the command: the major and the minor version.

rows.text: On an SB16, command FAh writes its second data byte into the 8051's memory at the address in its first.
On any other card the command is logged as unhandled and writes nothing.
On an SB16 the 8051 memory at addresses 20h and 30h receives dsp.last_cmd, before and after the command's own case.
Two data bytes follow the command.

rows.text: On an SB16, command F9h queues for the read the byte in the 8051's memory at the address in its data byte.
On any other card the command is logged as unhandled and queues no byte.
One data byte follows the command.
